title: FOCAL: A First-Order Carbon Model to Assess Processor Sustainability
problem: Processors consume substantial materials and energy resources throughout their lifetime, contributing to global warming. Computer architects lack a holistic framework to assess trade-offs between chip area, energy, and power consumption in terms of environmental footprint.
motivation: Reducing the environmental impact of computing is a critical grand challenge as processor resource consumption directly contributes to climate change.
method: FOCAL is a simplified carbon calculation method that measures environmental impact by looking at processor size, energy consumption, and power usage, then combines these into a single score called normalized carbon footprint (NCF)—normalized means you can fairly compare different chips. The model ranks typical processor design features as strongly, weakly, or less sustainable choices. Architects use this to understand which design decisions have the biggest impact on environmental footprint.
key_novelty: FOCAL is a simplified carbon model that combines chip area, energy, and power consumption using a normalized metric (NCF, or normalized carbon footprint) to holistically assess processor sustainability.
contributions: FOCAL: A parameterized first-order carbon model for processor sustainability assessment
Normalized Carbon Footprint (NCF) metric for guiding holistic processor optimization
Categorization of processor mechanisms by sustainability impact (strongly, weakly, less sustainable)
Design pathway for sustainable high-performance multicore processors
limitations: First-order model may not capture higher-order interactions and real-world variations in manufacturing, transportation, and end-of-life recycling processes.
